full_judgment:
SM Emdadul Hoque J: The petitioner after surrendering before this Court today in person filed this application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure praying for Anticipatory Bail in connection with ACC GR Case No. 47 of 2008 corresponding to Ramna Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 13-4-2008 under sections 26(2), 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and under section 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. 

 2. The learned Advocate Mr Helal Uddin Molla appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the petitioner is a retired Justice of this Court and later discharged his duties as Adviser of the Caretaker Government headed by Mr Professor Iajuddin Ahmed and now he is an aged person of 70 years with ailing health. The learned Advocate further submits that the allegations as brought against the petitioner in the FIR do not come under the mischief of section 26(2), 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and also under section 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007. He further submits that the FIR has been lodged at a belated stage on 13-4-2008 showing the commission of the offence on 16-11-2007. He further submits that in order to harass the petitioner by a vested quarter the said belated FIR has been lodged with false allegation and the proceeding has been initiated against the petitioner only to harass and malign the petitioner on political victimisation as he was an Adviser of the previous Caretaker Government. He further submits that the petitioner is not only an aged person with ailing health but is a respectable man in the society as a retired Justice of the Bangladesh Supreme Court having no chance of absconsion who will face the trial and the consequence of the case. The petitioner has surrendered before this Court today and prays for anticipatory bail only for avoiding the harassment which may be considered by this Court since the petitioner is on the same footing as with Mr Sadek Hossain Khoka against whom similar allegation was brought in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 10085 of 2008 and the bail was granted to him and also with Mr Saifur Rahman who was also granted bail against whom similar allegation alike the petitioner was brought. 

 3. The learned Deputy Attorney-General Ms Mubina Asaf in opposing the prayer for anticipatory bail submits that as the charge sheet has already been submitted against the petitioner in Ramna Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 13-4-2008 the petitioner may be directed to surrender before the trial Court and to pray for bail from the said Court. 

 4. We have heird the learned Advocate and the learned Deputy Attorney-General, perused the application for anticipatory bail and also the assertion made in the FIR. It appears that the petitioner was a Judge of the Bangladesh Supreme Court retired from the Appellate Division and has a respectable status in the society. He has also acted as an Adviser of the then Caretaker Government headed by Professor lajuddin Ahmed and complying the notice of the Anti-Corruption Commission the petitioner submitted his wealth statement before the Anti-Corruption Commission where from the commission has invented a discrepancy in his wealth statement and also other corruption committed by him during his tenure as Adviser of the Caretaker Government and lodged the instant case. The petitioner has retired from the Appellate Division at the age of 65 years and now he is running age of 70 years with ailing health as appears from his gesture before us. 

 6. In the result the application is allowed. Let the petitioner be enlarged on anticipatory bail in connection with ACC GR Case No. 47 of 2008 corresponding to Ramna Model Police Station Case No. 20 dated 13-4-2008 under sections 26(2), 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Act read with section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 and under section 15 of the Emergency Power Rules, 2007 now pending in the Court of Metropolitan Special Session Judge, Dhaka for a period of three months on furnishing adequate bail bond to the satisfaction of the trial Court. The petitioner is further directed to surrender before the trial Court within the said period.
